A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same dynamic weight grafting study. All 33 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original position and component grafting experiments across four language models, with additional dataset results, ablations, and token-probability examples in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds a Wikipedia finetuning experiment in Section 3.4 and a token-probability example in Appendix C.10.4.

M1.justification: Section 2, Algorithm 1, and Appendix B retain the same token-dependent component masks, parameter swapping and restoration, and KV-cache procedure. The Wikipedia experiment applies the existing method without introducing a new component.

E1.justification: v3 retains the three synthetic movie/actor relation datasets and adds Gemma finetuning on Wikipedia articles about films released after the model's release (Section 3.4). This extends coverage to non-templated finetuning text within the same movie-knowledge and relation-completion domain.

E2.justification: Corresponding position and component experiments retain their pretrained, supervised-finetuned, and task/relation-model comparisons. The new Wikipedia experiment reuses existing PRE/SFT controls and grafting configurations; no new comparison algorithm is evaluated.

E3.justification: The added experiment uses Gemma with twenty Wikipedia articles and five LLM-generated rephrases per article, reporting top-5 and top-50 accuracy. These are settings for a new experiment; the existing splits, model configurations, and finetuning settings in Appendix A.3 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 3.4 adds a targeted robustness check of whether localization patterns persist with non-templated finetuning text. Appendix C.10.4 adds a Gemma case showing common tokens dominating despite the target appearing in the top five. Existing position, component, unembedding, and finetuning analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The reference to three training runs in Appendix A.3.4's compute accounting is unchanged. v3 introduces no new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures; Figure 6 reports point accuracies.

E6.justification: Existing plotted values and token-probability examples are retained. New Figure 6 reports FE+LT versus SFT accuracy of 0.45 versus 0.50 at top-5 and 0.80 versus 0.80 at top-50 under the Wikipedia setting. Appendix C.10.4 adds an example with target Robert at 0.016 and common token a at 0.365.

T1.justification: The relation-completion definitions, weight-grafting equations, dynamic mask formulation, and Transformer-block expression are mathematically unchanged. Neither version adds a theorem or proof; the equation edits are typographical.

C1.justification: The two-pathway and recall-component localization claims remain. The conclusion now explicitly restricts the findings to single-hop relations and drops v2's closing suggestion of applications to model editing, narrowing the stated scope.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly acknowledges single-hop coverage and discusses wording, entity-order, and possible prior-exposure confounds for the Wikipedia experiment. Its future-work explanation also clarifies that alternative extraction can occur before the final token and pass information forward.

D1.justification: Section 3.4 adds article-selection and LLM-rephrasing details for the new experiment. Sections 1 and 7 change the listed code repository from knowledge-grafting to dynamic-weight-grafting. Existing pseudocode, hardware, hyperparameters, and training-time disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the references add Merullo, Eickhoff, and Pavlick's 2024 work, Language models implement simple word2vec-style vector arithmetic. The broader positioning relative to activation patching, weight grafting, and knowledge editing remains stable.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled Dynamic Weight Grafting: Localizing Finetuned Factual Knowledge in Transformers. Localized edits clarify the analysis framing, terminology, and conclusion; Sections 3.4 and C.10.4 are added, while the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds the two-panel Wikipedia Figure 6, moves Table 1 into Appendix A.2.1, and relocates Figures 2 and 4. Plot headings are incorporated into captions, and the author block and conference headers change. Existing plot contents are retained.

improvement.justification: The Wikipedia experiment provides useful evidence that the central localization pattern extends beyond v2's templated relation-learning data. Explicit single-hop qualifications and the added token-probability example also improve interpretive clarity. The gain is limited: the new experiment covers Gemma and twenty articles, with acknowledged wording, entity-order, and prior-exposure confounds.
